short: A Mongol reconnaissance force destroyed the combined armies of the Rus' princes and vanished.
full:
Jebe and Subutai had been sent after the fleeing Shah Muhammad II and, once he was dead, asked leave to ride on around the Caspian. They crossed the Caucasus, broke a Georgian army, and emerged on the steppe north of the Black Sea, where the Cuman khan Kotyan appealed to his son-in-law Mstislav the Bold for help.

On 31 May 1223 a coalition of Rus' princes and Cumans met them on the Kalka River, in what is now eastern Ukraine. The Mongols withdrew for several days, drawing the allies forward until their contingents were strung out and no longer in contact, then turned. Mstislav of Kiev fortified a camp on a hill, held for three days, and surrendered on terms that were not kept: he and other princes were crushed beneath a platform on which the victors dined. Perhaps a tenth of the Rus' army returned. Jebe and Subutai then rode home, and the principalities heard nothing more of the Mongols for fourteen years.
